summary: Connection pool exhaustion causing sustained 504 waves from API gateway
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 03:15 UTC we observed sustained waves of 504 Gateway Timeouts returned to customers in the dedicated environment. Impact: ~8% of requests to the customer's pinned model returned 504 over a 90-minute window, causing request retries and user-visible failures. Environment: Dedicated tenant (NimbusAnalytics) running in prod us-east-1, pinned to gpt-open-13b-v2. Initial symptom: API gateway returned 504 with upstream connection errors.

High level hypothesis: API gateway reported upstream connection pool exhaustion — idle connections were not being returned to the pool promptly because long-lived streaming sessions (some aborted by clients) did not fully release sockets on the serving-runtime side. This caused connection queues at the gateway to fill and new requests to be dropped with 504s until connections closed.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use a simulated client to open multiple streaming sessions to the customer's pinned model with intermittent client-side aborts (disconnect mid-stream).
2) Configure concurrency to exceed default gateway upstream connection limit (replay of production concurrency profile).
3) Observe that aborted streaming sessions leave connections in CLOSE_WAIT/half-open state in the runtime container until TCP timeout.
4) When active+half-open connections exceed gateway pool, new requests get 504.
logs:
Gateway logs (sample):
[2026-03-10T03:22:11Z] api-gw: upstream_connection_error (no available upstream connections) route=/v1/generate tenant=NimbusAnalytics
[2026-03-10T03:22:12Z] proxy: queued_requests=120 upstream_in_use=64 pool_capacity=64
Runtime container syslog (sample):
[2026-03-10T03:21:58Z] runtime: stream-session id=abc123 client-abort=true socket_state=CLOSE_WAIT
[2026-03-10T03:22:05Z] runtime: failed to detect client disconnect on stream id=def456; gc-ttl not triggered
investigation_notes:
- Triage: Alerting fired for elevated 504 rate for tenant NimbusAnalytics. Notified on-call SRE.
- Quick check: No code rollouts in the last 24h; autoscaler healthy.
- Observed correlation between spikes in aborted streaming sessions and 504 rate increases.
- Kernel/TCP metrics showed many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on runtime pods serving that tenant. Sockets lingered for default OS TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT timeout (~60s), tying up upstream slots.
- Reproduced in staging with a streaming-abort load test that simulates flaky clients: confirmed that runtime did not reliably close sockets when clients aborted mid-stream on certain code path (streaming proxy layer).
- Hypothesis refined: a rare code path in the streaming proxy failed to call the connection release logic when the client aborted before the runtime responded. This created transient leaks in the gateway upstream pool.
- Confirmed heap and FD counts on affected runtime pods increased during the window then recovered after connections aged out. No OOMs observed.
comments:
Priya Natarajan (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported 504s starting ~03:20 UTC. Confirmed scope and escalated to SRE.
Marco Hernandez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging. Simulated aborting streaming clients created CLOSE_WAIT sockets that were not released. Increasing gateway pool size reduced immediate 504s.
Jenna Park (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-10: Identified missing release call in streaming proxy when client disconnects during initial handshake. Preparing hotfix.
Alex Li (SRE) 2026-03-10: Temporarily increased upstream pool and reduced backend keepalive TTL to force earlier socket cleanup as mitigation.
NimbusAnalytics CS contact (Evelyn Torres) 2026-03-11: Confirmed error rate dropped and service is stable. Asked for root cause and fix ETA.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation steps executed:
- Emergency config change: api-gateway upstream pool size increased from 64 to 128 for the affected tenant route to reduce immediate 504s.
- Reduced runtime keepalive socket TTL to 10s to speed cleanup of half-open connections while hotfix was prepared.
- Deployed runtime hotfix (PR #1824): streaming proxy now calls connection.release() in all abort/exception codepaths and adds defensive socket close on abort.
- Rolled back temporary keepalive TTL change after confirming hotfix prevents leaks.
- Added a circuit-breaker rule to the gateway for per-tenant queued_requests to fail fast at a lower threshold and reduce tail impact.
resolution: Fixed in runtime (streaming proxy) and mitigated at gateway; monitoring added; customer notified.
follow_up_actions:
1) Postmortem: Schedule 1-hour postmortem with SRE, Runtime Eng, and Support. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/2026-03-10+SUP-87390+post-incident-notes
2) Add integration test that aborts streaming mid-request and asserts connection counts return to baseline.
3) Instrument per-connection release counters in runtime for early detection.
4) Update runbook: add immediate mitigation steps to increase upstream pool and reduce keepalive TTL for tenant-scoped outages.
5) Consider connection pool autoscaling or reserve headroom for dedicated tenants with streaming-heavy workloads.
